FAQ

Straight answers about what Aerobridge does today.

The product is in active development. These answers separate current capability from the roadmap.

Programs and access

What programs are available?

ICAO Aviation English and Pilot Licence Theory. The English program has six modules and 30 published lessons. Pilot Theory is live, with later lessons still being completed.

Can I use Aerobridge outside Chile?

Yes for the shared programs, especially ICAO Aviation English. However, Chile is the only active country pack. Do not rely on Aerobridge for another country's licensing requirements until that pack is published.

How do I create an account?

Use the learner sign-up page in the dashboard. Once your access is active, sign in and open Programs.

Is pricing published?

No. Billing, invoices and online payment plans are not connected. Contact Aerobridge for current access information.

Authorities and countries

What does the Chile DGAC pack include?

Current references for DAN 61 licensing, DAN 67 medical certification, DGAC exam-bank material, flight evaluation sheets and the licence guide. DAN 141 remains pending and is not presented as published content.

Are other country packs available?

Not yet. Additional countries are planned, but no names or dates are promised. A pack will be published only after its authority, source documents and licence pathways are verified.

Is there a standalone FAA course?

No. Pilot Licence Theory contains labelled United States reference material, but Aerobridge does not currently list a standalone FAA preparation or certification program.

Assessment and certification

Is Aerobridge an official test or certification provider?

No. Aerobridge provides preparation and practice. It does not issue licences or certify ICAO levels. Confirm approved tests, endorsements and validity with your authority.

How does Aviation English practice scoring work?

The current scorecards are previews used to demonstrate the product flow. They are not official assessments and are not calculated from recorded audio.

What does ICAO Level 4 mean?

Level 4 is the operational minimum across the six language proficiency descriptors. The final official rating, validity and retesting rules depend on the approved assessment and authority.

Still unsure whether the current scope fits?

Send your country, authority and licence goal. We will answer directly.
